params.title: Satellite
params.subtitle: Iridium, COSPAS-SARSAT, Inmarsat and GPS compared by orbit altitude, frequencies, services and antennas.

scenes.narration: This lesson compares 4 satellite systems: Iridium, COSPAS-SARSAT, Inmarsat, and GPS, the Global Positioning System. For each one, we'll look at how high it orbits, which frequencies it uses, what services it provides, and what antennas it needs. We'll start low, with Iridium, a low Earth orbit system.

params.title: Iridium: low Earth orbit
items: Orbits at 485 miles, far below the geostationary Inmarsat satellites
Uses the 1616–1626 MHz band for telephone and messaging
Digital voice and data at 2.4 kbps

onScreen: Digital voice and data at 2.4 kbps
scenes.narration: Iridium is a satellite communications system in low Earth orbit. Its satellites orbit at an altitude of 485 miles, far below the geostationary Inmarsat satellites. Iridium uses the 1616 to 1626 megahertz band for telephone and messaging. Its services are digital voice and data at 2.4 kilobits per second. There is no analog voice on Iridium.

params.title: Iridium: true or false?
rows: The keyed answer: choose it on the exam
Really about 400 km, or 250 miles, across

onScreen: For the exam: 48 spot beams, 30-mile footprint
scenes.narration: The exam asks which statement about Iridium is true. For the exam, the keyed answer is: there are 48 spot beams per satellite, with a footprint of 30 miles in diameter. Choose it. The 48 beams are real, but each one is really about 400 kilometers, or about 250 miles, across. Watch for a wrong choice: Iridium is not 48 satellites in 4 orbital planes. It uses 66 active satellites in 6 near-polar planes, inclined 86.4 degrees, with an orbital period of about 100 minutes.

blocks.label: Ship's position
blocks.note: Doppler shift at several orbit points

onScreen: Position from Doppler shift at several orbit points
scenes.narration: Now COSPAS-SARSAT. Its main function is to monitor 406 megahertz for distress calls from EPIRBs, emergency position-indicating radio beacons, and relay them to ground stations called local user terminals. How does it find the ship in distress? By measuring the Doppler shift of the 406 megahertz signal, taken at several different points in the satellite's orbit. Only beacons with built-in GPS send their own coordinates.

Inmarsat satellites orbit at an altitude of 22,177 miles, in geostationary orbit above the equator. The system is laid out by ocean region. AOR-E, the Atlantic Ocean Region East, is at 15.5 degrees west. AOR-W, the Atlantic Ocean Region West, is at 54 degrees west. POR, the Pacific Ocean Region, is at 178 degrees east. And IOR, the Indian Ocean Region, is at 64.5 degrees east.

params.title: Inmarsat coverage
items: Coverage to vessels in nearly all of the world's navigable waters
Geostationary above the equator: not in polar orbit
Polar regions above about 70° latitude are missed
So the coverage is not truly global

onScreen: Misses the poles above about 70° latitude
scenes.narration: Where do these satellites reach? Inmarsat geostationary satellites provide coverage to vessels in nearly all of the world's navigable waters. But they are not in polar orbit. Sitting above the equator, they miss the polar regions above about 70 degrees latitude. So Inmarsat coverage is not truly global, and a choice claiming a polar orbit or true global coverage is wrong.

callouts.label: Inmarsat-C SES antenna: omnidirectional, no aiming or stabilization
Inmarsat-B voice: CODECs digitize the voice signal
Obstruction, such as a mast, blocking the signal on a certain course
Satellite on a low elevation, below the horizon
Travel beyond the effective radius of the satellite

onScreen: Mast obstruction on a certain course
scenes.narration: Now the ship's equipment. The Inmarsat-C SES, or ship earth station, antenna is omnidirectional, so it needs no aiming or stabilization. For voice communications through an Inmarsat-B terminal, CODECs, or coder-decoders, are used to digitize the voice signal. And 3 conditions can make Inmarsat-B communications impossible: an obstruction, such as a mast, blocking the signal when the vessel steers a certain course; a satellite on a low elevation, below the horizon; or travel beyond the effective radius of the satellite. Any of these will do it, so the answer is all of these.

blocks.label: Land earth station
blocks.note: Stores the message, then forwards it

onScreen: Ship earth station sends a routine or distress message
Land earth station stores, then forwards
scenes.narration: Inmarsat-C is a store-and-forward system that provides routine and distress communications. A message from the ship earth station goes up to the satellite and down to a land earth station, which stores it and then forwards it to the recipient. So Inmarsat-C is not real-time telex, and it does not carry voice.

params.title: Inmarsat-B versus Inmarsat-C
rows: Routine and distress messages, no voice

onScreen: B: voice 16 kbps, fax 14.4 kbps, data 64/54 kbps
scenes.narration: Compare Inmarsat-B with Inmarsat-C. Inmarsat-B services are voice at 16 kilobits per second, fax at 14.4 kilobits per second, and high-speed data at 64 slash 54 kilobits per second, all delivered in real time rather than store-and-forward. Inmarsat-C carries routine and distress messages, but no voice. The antennas differ too. Inmarsat-C antennas are small and omnidirectional, while Inmarsat-B antennas are larger and directional.

params.title: Inmarsat-M, mini-M and high-speed data
items: Inmarsat-M: voice at 6.2 kbps, data at 2.4 kbps, fax at 2.4 kbps, and e-mail
Mini-M: a satellite system using spot beams for small craft communications
High-speed data at 64/54 kbps: Inmarsat-B, M4 and Fleet
Their high-gain directional antennas make it possible

onScreen: Inmarsat-M: voice 6.2 kbps, data and fax 2.4 kbps, e-mail
Mini-M: spot beams for small craft
64/54 kbps data: B, M4 and Fleet
scenes.narration: 2 more Inmarsat services. Inmarsat-M provides voice at 6.2 kilobits per second, data at 2.4 kilobits per second, fax at 2.4 kilobits per second, and e-mail. The Inmarsat mini-M system is a satellite system utilizing spot beams to provide for small craft communications. Finally, which systems offer high-speed data at 64 slash 54 kilobits per second? Inmarsat-B, M4 and Fleet, because their high-gain directional antennas support it.

onScreen: GPS: 12,554 miles, about once every 12 hours
scenes.narration: Now GPS. GPS satellites orbit at an altitude of 12,554 miles, circling the Earth about once every 12 hours. Here's how that compares. Iridium sits far below, in low Earth orbit at 485 miles. Inmarsat sits far above, in geostationary orbit at 22,177 miles. So from low to high, it's Iridium, then GPS, then Inmarsat.

params.title: The GPS constellation
items: 24 GPS satellites normally in operation, 4 in each orbital plane, plus spares
6 orbital planes, equally spaced, inclined about 55° to the equator
4 satellites must be received for complete position and time
The receiver solves latitude, longitude, altitude and its own clock error

scenes.narration: 24 GPS satellites are normally in operation, 4 in each orbital plane, with extra satellites kept as spares. There are 6 orbital planes, equally spaced and inclined about 55 degrees to the equator, so GPS orbits are neither polar nor geosynchronous. How many satellites must be received to provide complete position and time? 4. The receiver has to solve for latitude, longitude, altitude, and its own clock error, and that takes 4 satellites.

The GPS transmitted frequencies are 1227.6 megahertz and 1575.4 megahertz. Don't mix them up with the other satellite frequencies in this lesson. Just above GPS is Iridium's 1616 to 1626 megahertz band for telephone and messaging. And far below is 406 megahertz, which COSPAS-SARSAT monitors for distress calls from EPIRBs.

blocks.label: Reference station
blocks.note: Precisely surveyed: measures the GPS error

onScreen: Reference station at a precisely surveyed location
Correction factors to the ship's receiver
scenes.narration: Finally, DGPS, or Differential GPS. It is a system to provide additional correction factors to improve position accuracy. A reference station sits at a precisely surveyed location. Because it knows exactly where it is, it can measure the error in the GPS signals it receives, and it broadcasts correction factors. A ship's receiver applies them to improve its position accuracy.
